title: Counting Our Day
text:
My class has twenty students. There are thirty chairs in the room. Our teacher has forty pencils in her bag. She says fifty is half of one hundred.

On Sunday, my family went to the park. We counted sixty birds and seventy trees. My sister counted ninety ducks at the lake. Next time, we want to count one hundred animals.

questions.text: How many students are in the class?
How many ducks did the sister count?
Why does the family want to count one hundred animals next time?
options: They want to try a new challenge.

questions.text: What can we infer about the family on Sunday?
options: They stayed at home all day.
They did not see any animals.

vocabulary.definition: people who are learning in a class or school
seats for one person, with a back
water birds with short legs and flat beaks
living creatures that are not plants or people

paragraph_translations: Minha turma tem vinte alunos. Há trinta cadeiras na sala. Nossa professora tem quarenta lápis na bolsa. Ela diz que cinquenta é a metade de cem.
No domingo, minha família foi ao parque. Contamos sessenta pássaros e setenta árvores. Minha irmã contou noventa patos no lago. Da próxima vez, queremos contar cem animais.
